_: MLP-split crossover, quick tier: does a crossover exist on this rig, and
roughly where. Two arms, one concentration vector.
WHY THIS IS MEASURED AND NOT LOOKED UP. Concentrating dense-MLP units on
the compute-strong rank buys prefill per prompt token and costs decode per
output token. Both slopes depend on the card mix, the interconnect, the
model and which quantisation lane each rank ends up on, so the ratio where
they cancel is a property of THIS machine. Numbers from another rig are
shown as that rig's finding and never used here.
WHAT ONE INVOCATION COVERS. A study run measures ONE point of the
parameter space with all arms interleaved. The point below is the prefill
half at 4000 prompt tokens. Cover the rest with the same file and a point
override:
phase=random-ids output_tokens=1   prompt_tokens=1000
phase=random-ids output_tokens=1   prompt_tokens=4000   (this file)
phase=random-ids output_tokens=1   prompt_tokens=11000
phase=random     output_tokens=256 prompt_tokens=400
TIME. 2 noise-floor boots + 1 interleaved repeat over 2 arms = 4 boots per
point, 4 points = 16 boots. At ~3.5 min per boot (boot, weight load,
settle, 10-20 s of load) that is ~55 min.
WHAT THE QUICK TIER CANNOT DO. The floor is two boots wide, so a
difference close to it is not resolvable, and one concentration vector
cannot produce an envelope -- it answers whether the effect exists and
roughly where it turns, not which vector to pick.
CACHE BYPASS IS THE RESULT, NOT A DETAIL. The prefill points use
--dataset-name random-ids so every request carries input ids no other
request has; a repeated prompt is served from the radix cache and the
measurement becomes a cache measurement. Check #cached-token: 0 on every
prefill chunk in the server log and record it with the result. The
positive control is the same prompt sent twice in one boot.
DECODE IS MEASURED ON NATURAL TEXT. Raw ms per output token over random
ids is acceptance-driven: it has produced a 4.7x phantom depth term and a
negative step time. Report ms per speculative step and carry the accept
length beside it.
THE KV OWNERSHIP VECTOR IS PINNED in every arm, so the weight split is the
only thing that moves. Without that pin two levers move at once and
neither is attributable.
PATHS COME FROM THE ENVIRONMENT. model_path, the draft model and
python_exe are written as ${MODEL_ROOT:-<MODEL_ROOT>}/... and
${VENV:-<VENV>}/bin/python; load_study expands them. Source your local
rig env file before running. The defaults are placeholders on purpose --
an unsourced run fails on a visibly bogus path instead of booting
against whatever tree this file's author happened to have.
